plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.

conservative.read: This plan aims for lower, steadier returns around 1.5% per month. The focus is on reducing risk and maintaining a cash buffer, leading to potentially smaller drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Reduce exposure in 2x AI/Software (METU) and 2x Semiconductor (MUU).
Trim Income ETF (QQQI) to 20% to manage concentration.

This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly returns. It seeks growth by trimming leverage and concentration while adding a diversified name. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly returns, accepting higher risk. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrated positions, which can lead to significant gains but also larger, faster drawdowns. Daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs can impact performance.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta single names (METU, MUU).
Increase Income ETF (QQQI) to 30% for higher yield focus.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly returns. The strategy is to park capital in income-generating assets and broad indices for stability. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
